key_insight: Metal Sandbox combines isolated agent workspaces, native macOS execution, and command scheduling to support concurrent GPU-coding agents on Apple Silicon. It targets GPU idle time between model requests, development commands, and kernel execution.
problem_solved: Agents generating Apple Metal kernels need native tools and safe concurrent execution, but their intermittent GPU use can leave accelerator capacity underutilized.
method: Restrict file access per instance to isolate concurrent agent sessions.
Execute development commands natively on macOS for Apple Metal workflows.
Use command-level scheduling to coordinate concurrent workloads and target idle GPU capacity.
impact: The infrastructure could make training and evaluating Metal-kernel-generating agents more resource-efficient on Apple Silicon. The supplied abstract is truncated, so specific scheduling mechanisms and measured performance gains are not available.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: isolated agent workspaces connected to native macOS tools and a shared GPU.
Session timeline: alternating model requests, development commands, and GPU execution, highlighting idle gaps.
Scheduling diagram: commands from multiple agents feeding a shared execution queue.
Icon trio: file-access lock, macOS terminal, and Apple Silicon GPU.
paper_title: Metal Sandbox: Isolated Execution and Command Scheduling for GPU Coding Agents on Apple Silicon
paper_authors: Haozhe Wang, Lina Chen, Fanqi Wan, Qi Han, Yinmin Zhang
